title: Rich-message contract: FormattedSender + AttachmentSender + fake
description:
Foundation contract tick — internal/operator only (channel.go, fake.go + tests); do NOT touch telegram/ or cmd/.

Additive channel capabilities (operator.Channel itself unchanged — model on the existing optional-interface precedent set by operator.Adopter, so FakeChannel and telegram.Channel opt in and other implementers do not break):
- FormattedSender: SendFormatted(ctx, FormattedText) error where FormattedText{Text string, Format Format} with Format one of FormatMarkdownLite (bold/italic/code/links subset expressible in BOTH Telegram HTML and Slack Block Kit — document the mapping in godoc per element) — keep the enum open for future formats. Plain Send stays plain-text (54v review decision) and its contract text must not change.
- AttachmentSender: SendAttachment(ctx, Attachment) (MessageRef, error) with Attachment{Path string, Caption string, Kind AttachmentKind (KindAuto|KindDocument|KindPhoto), Gate bool} — Gate=true means approve/reject buttons under the attachment; returning MessageRef lets the ask engine treat a gated attachment exactly like a delivered question.
- AskDeliver gains nothing — a photo+gate ask is composed by the caller: SendAttachment(Gate:true) then the pending entry adopts that MessageRef (verify the engine's Adopter path can register it; if a small engine hook is needed — e.g. Engine.RegisterDelivered(tick, ref, q) — add it here with tests through FakeChannel).
- FakeChannel implements both, with recorders (Formatted() []FormattedText, Attachments() []Attachment) and scriptable gate events on attachment refs.

Test cases: FormattedText round-trip through fake; attachment kinds incl KindAuto resolution by extension (.png/.jpg→photo, else document); gated attachment produces a ref the engine can await on (press resolves like a normal gate, human provenance unchanged); interface assertions that a channel WITHOUT the new interfaces still compiles and degrades (capability probe helper, e.g. operator.SupportsAttachments(ch) bool).
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/...
